Oncall Bot: Pager alert - elevated 5xx rates observed for customer velarium on dedicated cluster ded-cluster-7. Metric: gateway_5xx_rate > 8% sustained for 3m. Paging on-call (priority: P1).

Marta Ruiz: ack, I'm taking first touch. seeing spikes in the dashboard. paxq showing queue depth increasing on region-us-east-1.

Devon Ng: I'm online. can you dump recent gateway logs and a sample of 5xx traces?

Marta Ruiz: grabbing logs now. looks noisy: lots of long tail latency from one tenant id=velarium-tenant-42? but customer is Velarium — they have traffic, not sure about noisy neighbor yet.

Marta Ruiz: paste logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:21Z ded-gateway-7 ERROR request_id=abc123 status=502 backend_err="kv_paging_timeout" tenant=velarium-42 latency=2800ms
2026-03-15T02:10:22Z ded-gateway-7 ERROR request_id=abc124 status=503 backend_err="gpu_queue_overflow" tenant=tenant-x9 latency=3005ms
2026-03-15T02:10:23Z ded-gateway-7 ERROR request_id=abc125 status=504 backend_err="kv_eviction" tenant=tenant-x9 latency=15000ms
```

Priya Shah: that looks like mixed signals — velarium-42 and tenant-x9. tenant-x9 seems to be exhausting KV and GPU queues, causing backpressure across the node. noisy neighbor suspicion.

Elias Turner: +1. Check node allocation: ded-cluster-7 has 16 nodes, but only 2 nodes in az-a are handling a lot of tenant-x9 affinity. running `redwoodctl cluster inspect ded-cluster-7 --nodes` now.

Devon Ng: while Elias inspects, we should protect Velarium traffic. Options: 1) route Velarium to warm standby pool in us-west-2 2) apply per-tenant egress throttle for tenant-x9 3) evict noisy tenant from shared pool. Which is fastest?

Marta Ruiz: fastest is route Velarium -> fallback pool. I can flip routing policy for velarium to region fallback for the next 15m. will that break sticky KV? small risk, but better than customer errors.

SRE Pager: handoff note: if you route, confirm model cache warmup because Velarium uses long context models. set `--warm-prefix` to avoid cold-start.

Marta Ruiz: doing `redwoodctl routes update --customer velarium --target fallback-us-west --duration 15m --warm-prefix true` now.

Oncall Bot: Command executed by Marta Ruiz at 2789990065: routes update accepted.

Marta Ruiz: routing flip completed. Velarium requests now going to fallback-us-west-2. monitoring.

Velarium Support (bot): From Velarium support: we've received error reports from our app users starting ~02:09 UTC. Can you confirm mitigation and ETA?

Marta Ruiz: @Velarium Support we just routed your production traffic to a fallback pool in us-west-2. Expect brief connection warmups (~20–45s) then progressive recovery. We'll follow up with status in 5m.

Priya Shah: telemetry shows Velarium 5xx down from 9% -> 1.2% over last 60s. good sign. however node-level KV eviction still high (tenant-x9).

Elias Turner: found noisy tenant: tenant-x9 has a job with sustained large batch decoding causing GPU queue starvation. host list: node-07, node-08 in az-a. I can cordon node-07 and drain tenant-x9 off those nodes.

Devon Ng: before draining, let's avoid mass evictions that might spike other queues. propose: apply rate-limit on tenant-x9 (limit concurrent requests to 20), then gradually drain the processes. use `redwoodctl tenant throttle tenant-x9 --concurrency 20`

Elias Turner: applying throttle now.

Oncall Bot: Command executed by Elias Turner at 2789990180: tenant throttle applied.

Priya Shah: KV eviction rate immediately drops 60% after throttle. queue depth normalizing. good.

Marta Ruiz: Velarium 5xx now ~0.4% and latency recovered to baseline. I'm going to keep the fallback route for 10 more minutes and then cut back if stable.

Velarium Support (bot): Confirming users are reporting restored service. thanks for the rapid response.

SRE Pager: handoff plan: primary SRE shift retains ownership for 15m of observation, then hand to oncall-night (Devon) at 2789990360. Make sure we note mitigation steps and follow-up action items.

Devon Ng: taking handoff at 2789990360. I'll follow up on permanent fixes: either tenant isolation for tenant-x9, enforce autoscaling on that customer's reserved pool, or stricter per-tenant concurrency limits cluster-wide.

Marta Ruiz: quick incident notes for postmortem: timeline, root cause noisy tenant-x9 causing KV evictions & GPU queue overflow; mitigations applied = immediate routing for Velarium, throttle + drain noisy tenant, node cordon planned; customer notified.

Elias Turner: new action item: infra to add a quota guard in placement that prevents >40% of a node's active slots being consumed by a single tenant. filing ticket INF-1279.

Priya Shah: also add alert tweak: split gateway_5xx_rate by tenant tag so paging can target noisy tenant earlier. filing ticket SRE-3421.

Devon Ng: closing P1 alert to monitoring (keeping incident open for postmortem). mark customer-impact: Velarium briefly degraded for ~3 minutes, impact classification: partial (some users saw errors then recovered).

Oncall Bot: Incident acknowledged closed by Devon Ng at 2789990360 (alert suppressed).

Marta Ruiz: thanks team. I'll draft the incident summary and ping CS to send a follow-up note to Velarium. :thumbsup:
